summary: gateway-preflight recognises the OpenClaw 2026.10.9 config lock name state.<hash>.lock (besides 2026.9.x gateway.<hash>.lock), so a stale lock left by a stopped 10.9 Gateway is quarantined reversibly as before instead of refusing every start with config_lock_ambiguous.
reason: S24 01/11 22:35 UTC: during the rollback of companion-deploy 9862fd25 the runtime restart stopped the 10.9 Gateway; every start then failed with 'gateway lock preflight refused recovery: count 0, config_lock_ambiguous' although the lock owner was dead and the port closed, leaving the Gateway down until the two stale lock files were quarantined by hand.
rollback: Revert this commit and redeploy the previous commit with companion-deploy.sh; a stale 10.9 lock then blocks Gateway starts again.

tests.name: installer/termux-lite/test-gateway-preflight.py (ci.yml)
tests.evidence: 17 tests: the 10.9 layout (state.<hash>.lock, no .sqlite sibling) is stale_recoverable and quarantined, a live 10.9 owner is never reclaimed, both layouts for one config stay ambiguous; the 3 new tests fail on the previous preflight.

architecture.reason: Same preflight owner and same reversible quarantine; only the recognised lock file names grow.

limitations: Why the 10.9 Gateway left its locks on that stop is not established here; the preflight now recovers them either way.
